THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 06.07.2024 passed in MVC No.223/2022 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-IV, Davanagere, for enhancing the compensation.
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.1/Insurance Company.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. The petitioner/injured claimant met with an accident on 14.01.2022 and filed petition before the Tribunal for compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.

The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of NC: 2026:KHC:13884 HC-KAR Rs.5,53,070/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of filing the petition till the date of deposit.
Being aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is filed.
4. It is stated that the petitioner/injured was aged 24 years and was doing agricultural work.
He was also working as a tractor driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was hospitalized as an inpatient for 15 days.
The doctor assessed the permanent disability at 30%.
But the Tribunal has considered only 10% disability.
The petitioner had produced Ex.P.19-driving licence to prove his age, but the Tribunal has not considered the same and taken the multiplier as '17' instead of '18'.
It is further stated that the amounts awarded under the other heads are meagre.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Though it is stated that the petitioner/injured was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, he has not filed any income proof.
As he met with an accident in the year 2022, his notional income is to be taken as Rs.15,500/- per month, as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As per the driving licence produced and marked as NC: 2026:KHC:13884 HC-KAR Ex.P.19, the petitioner was born in the year 1997 and met with the accident on 14.01.2022.
Therefore, he was aged 24 years as on the date of the accident.
Accordingly, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '18'.

The petitioner/injured sustained the following injuries:
"1. Mandible fracture 2. Lacerated wound over the chin.

sentences.text: After discharge he was regularly following an outpatient basis.
In the parasymphosyis (left) and angle of mandible.
Mouth opening is painful and restricted unable to approximate teeth of upper and lower jaw.

On examination:
 Tenderness present over parasymphysis of mandible  Tenderness over angle of mandible  Occlusion is deranged  X-ray shows implant in situ with mal-union Opinion:
 Mal-occlusion unable to approximate upper and lower jaw teeth 25%
Chronic pain interfering with restriction 5%."
Therefore, the doctor assessed the permanent disability at 30% after clinical and radiological examination.
The Tribunal NC: 2026:KHC:13884 HC-KAR has rightly considered 1/3rd of the same as 10% to the whole body.

Accordingly, the loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.3,34,800/-
(15,500  12  18  10%).
6.
The petitioner/injured has incurred Rs.1,16,869/- towards medical expenses and the said amount is confirmed.
He was hospitalized for a period of 10 days.

Considering the nature of the injuries,
period of hospitalization and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The petitioner/injured might not have attended any other work at least for a period of three months.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.46,500/- (15,500x3) is awarded towards loss of income during the laid-up period.

7. Thus in all, compensation awarded by this Court is as below:

ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

iii. The claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.6,08,169/- along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization, instead of Rs.5,53,070/-
granted by the tribunal.
iv. Respondent No.1/Insurance Company has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal.
Therefore, respondent No.1/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.55,099/- along with the interest at the rate of 6% within one month from the date of this order.
v. On such deposit, petitioner is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on the same.
